title: Макс спасает ужин  (Max Saves the Dinner Service)

segments.t: Out in the dining room, Nagiyev impatiently demands his tartare while Aleksandr scrambles alone at the pass. Returning to the empty kitchen, Max sets his personal feelings aside and teams up with the new chef on sauces and soups to save the evening service.
Так, иди сюда, будешь помогать мне.
Ты как раз вовремя, у нас полно заказов.
Ты на холодном соусах, я на горячем супах.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Where is my tartare?' Vika raises the pitch on 'tartare' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Dmitry answers right away.
'The boy went out first.' The grammar packs 'boy' and 'to go out' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'No panic, we keep working.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'without' and finishing on 'to work'.
Так, иди сюда, будешь помогать мне.
'All right, come over here, you are going to help me.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'like this' and 'go' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
'No, I wash the dishes.' The meaning hinges on 'not' working together with 'my' in spoken Russian.
'You are going to help me. No.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'will you?' before landing on 'not'.
Ты как раз вовремя, у нас полно заказов.
'You are just in time, we are swamped with orders.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.
'Wait, where is everybody?' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'all' in spoken Russian.
'I do not know.' Vika anchors the line on 'not', while 'know' completes the thought.
'All right, let us roll.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'let's go' covers a group or the polite 'you'. Vika answers right away.
Ты на холодном соусах, я на горячем супах.
'You take the cold sauces, I am on the hot soups.' The grammar packs 'you' and 'soup' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Okay, pepper.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'like this' and 'pepper' in a few short words.
'What a crazy rush that was.' Notice how Russian expresses 'such' and 'was' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Так, иди сюда, будешь помогать мне.
Ты как раз вовремя, у нас полно заказов.
Ты на холодном соусах, я на горячем супах.
That wraps up this scene as returning to the deserted kitchen as Nagiyev demands his steak tartare, Max steps in to help Aleksandr power through the mountain of dinner orders. Until next time!
